pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: scripts/hybrid-bench/materialize-tags.ts:117 The materializer, sole writer of the derived `vote_tag` read model, only upserts answered rows and retracts nothing, so on a re-run a vote the model no longer answers (or one since voided, filtered at line 98) keeps its earlier tag even though the run reports it as left untagged, and no parity check exists to notice.

techniques.evidence: scripts/hybrid-bench/materialize-tags.ts:117 vote_tag is a stored read model (store.ts calls it DERIVED, recomputable), but the recompute is upsert-only: `VoteTagRepository` has no delete and a repo-wide search found no `delete from vote_tag` outside an instrument.test.ts parser string, so the recompute cannot be the repair. No parity or coverage check against vote_event was found, and no propagation contract is declared where the model is defined.

scripts/hybrid-bench/materialize-tags.ts:15 The context's only store contact is this typed surface; a search of scripts/hybrid-bench for query/sql/select found only prompts, comments and a local `Query` interface.

pairs.registryProposal: read-models-and-projections assumes a deterministic recomputation: its parity check 'recomputes and compares', which is ill-defined when the derivation is an LLM call that can answer differently per run. The technique could name what parity means for a model-derived read model, for example source-set parity (every stored row still maps to an eligible source row, and uncovered sources are counted) plus sampled re-classification agreement.
